items.title: Medicos warn against craze for fairness after 17-year-old Keralam girl diagnosed with kidney disorder
points: Medical experts say that the use of fairness creams containing heavy metals such as mercury to lighten the skin is emerging as a major health hazard that can lead to serious conditions such as kidney failure if not diagnosed early.

Lab tests had confirmed 1.25% mercury in the cosmetic product, according to the hospital sources.

items.title: Vice President urges graduates to embrace lifelong learning, contribute to nation-building
points: Radhakrishnan on Saturday (November 21, 2026) urged graduating students to pursue excellence with integrity, embrace lifelong learning and contribute to nation-building, saying that professional success must be accompanied by strong character and ethical…
He was speaking at the convocation ceremony of Symbiosis International (Deemed to be University) in Pune.

It is a collective mission involving citizens, educational institutions, businesses and communities,” he said, expressing confidence in the role of young professionals in achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047.
Highlighting India’s expansion in higher education over the past decade, the Vice President said the number of universities had increased from 760 in 2014-15 to more than 1,400.
Higher education enrolment had also increased from 3.4 crore to over 4.5 crore students, he said.

The Vice President also highlighted the growing participation of women in higher education, describing their increasing presence among graduates and medal winners as a visible sign of Nari Shakti and women’s empowerment.

items.title: Kerala-Linked Drug Racket Busted In Mumbai, Nigerian Man Among 2 Arrested
points: A Nigerian national suspected of running a major interstate drug trafficking network and his Indian wife have been arrested in Mumbai by a special team of Kerala Police.
Investigators say the couple controlled an MDMA distribution network supplying drugs to Kerala and Karnataka and were preparing to flee to Nigeria after transferring their proceeds abroad.
The accused have been identified as Ikechukwu Paul Ogbonna (40), a Nigerian national, and his wife Aarthi (42), a Mumbai resident.
The arrests were made in Ulwe, in the Mumbai metropolitan region, by a special investigation team led by Kondotty Police Inspector Sangeeth Punathil.
The investigation began on June 26 with a seemingly routine drug seizure in Malappuram district, when police recovered MDMA from Ratheesh (38), a resident of Thattaramchola House in Aroor, Kondotty.
What began as a local narcotics case eventually led investigators to an interstate supply network operating out of Maharashtra.
According to police, Ogbonna arrived in India approximately 15 years ago and married Aarthi, a Mumbai native, eight years ago.

items.title: "No Takers For Railways In Meghalaya": Chief Minister Conrad Sangma
points: There are no takers for the railway project in the eastern part of Meghalaya, with Shillong remaining one of the few state capitals in the country yet to be connected to the national railway network, said Chief Minister Conrad Sangma.

The Chief Minister has warned that the railway project could be pushed back by another decade or two as the Centre seeks the return of funds allocated for the stalled project in the Khasi-Jaintia Hills region.

Opposition from various organisations and stakeholders, driven largely by concerns over illegal immigration, demands for a mechanism to check illegal infiltration and the implementation of the Inner Line Permit (ILP), has kept the project in limbo.
With no one willing to accept railway connectivity without adequate safeguards, the Meghalaya government has initiated discussions with the Union government over returning the allocated funds.

The project now faces an uncertain future, caught between public opposition, demands for stronger protection against illegal infiltration and the Centre's insistence that unutilised funds be returned.

items.title: 4 Arrested, Stolen SUV Recovered Days After Gunpoint Robbery In Punjab's Pathankot
points: Four men have been arrested five days after a gunpoint carjacking in Punjab's Pathankot district, and a stolen SUV has been recovered, police said.
The prime suspect, Surjeet Singh, alias Sheena, was arrested in Vadodara with help from Gujarat Police.
The carjacking took place at around 9:30 pm on Sunday, November 15, at Downtown Mall 44 on the Pathankot-Jammu National Highway in Sujanpur.
The complainant, 40-year-old Praveen Singh of Bamial, had driven the vehicle owner's family to the complex.
While he was waiting inside the white Mahindra XUV500 (registration number PB35AA-9902), an armed man wearing a black headscarf approached him.
Given Pathankot's sensitive security history, the incident triggered a high alert across Punjab, Jammu and Kashmir, and Himachal Pradesh.

items.title: Pranab Doley | Confronting the State
points: Pranab Doley, 40, describes himself as a first-generation learner.
He graduated in Arts from Visva-Bharati University at Santiniketan in 2009 and earned a Master’s in Social Welfare from Mumbai’s Tata Institute of Social Sciences two years later.

Rather than pursue a conventional career, he turned to grassroots organising, helping found and lead bodies such as Jeepal Krishak Shramik Sangha (JKSS), a farmers’ rights group, and the All Kaziranga Affected Communities’ Rights Committee.

His fight for indigenous land rights in Assam has repeatedly brought him into confrontation with the State government, the latest ending in a 118-day detention under the National Security Act (NSA) for opposing a luxury hotel project near Kaziranga…
For Mr. Doley, it was another chapter in a long history of arrests connected to his activism.

items.title: India's Maize Exports To Vietnam Surge 341 Times On Record Domestic Supplies
points: India's maize exports to Vietnam have surged this year as a bumper domestic harvest and weak prices pushed traders to seek overseas markets, but the sharp rise in volumes has not translated into a proportional increase in export earnings.
Vietnamese government data show India exported 341 times more maize to Vietnam till October 2026 than during the same period a year earlier.
However, the value of those shipments rose only 59-fold, highlighting the steep discounts at which Indian corn is being sold in international markets.

According to the Vietnamese government, Indian maize that fetched about $1,447 a tonne during the corresponding period last year was sold this year at around $250 a tonne, a drop of roughly 83 per cent.
In a July 2026 update, Vietnam noted that import volumes from India had surged more than 310 times, while import value rose only about 45 times because of a sharp fall in prices.

items.title: School Reunion, Relationship, Jealousy: What Led To Tamil Nadu Double Murder
points: A labourer has been arrested for the murder of his former schoolmate whom he had allegedly been dating since last year, and the man he believed she had recently grown close to.
The double murder occurred in the Tirupattur district of Tamil Nadu yesterday.
The accused was identified as Sanjay Gandhi, who went to the same school in Tiruvannamalai district as Malini, one of the two victims.
The double murder has also triggered a political confrontation over the law-and-order situation in Tamil Nadu.
Former deputy chief minister and Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin has criticised the TVK government and demanded that Chief Minister Vijay take responsibility for law and order.
The Opposition has been criticising Vijay's government over what it has described as a deterioration in law and order and a rise in violent crimes across Tamil Nadu.
Opposition parties had earlier raised concerns after 13 murders were reported across the state during Diwali.

items.title: BJP Warns Its Bengal Leaders Against Defying Party Directives
points: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national general secretary and central observer Sunil Bansal on Friday issued a stern warning to party leaders and workers over organisational discipline, making it clear that no one, irrespective of their position, would be…

Bansal was addressing a meeting at the BJP's party office in Kolkata, attended by district presidents, divisional in-charges, party officials and state BJP president Shamik Bhattacharya, among others.
During the meeting, Bansal cautioned party members against conduct that could force the organisation to initiate disciplinary action.
He stressed that disciplinary measures would apply to everyone, from ordinary party workers to MLAs, MPs and ministers.
The warning comes amid complaints of internal factionalism and instances of party members publicly speaking against their own leaders and ministers.

A leader who attended Friday's meeting, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the senior leadership had warned that action could be taken against those found violating party discipline, even by bypassing the organisational structure.
